We perform the first three-dimensional measurement of the amplitudes of $B\to \psi(2S) K^*$ and $B\to \chi_{c1} K^*$ decays and update our previous measurement for $B\to J/\psi K^*$. We use a data sample collected with the BaBar detector at the PEP2 storage ring, corresponding to 232 million $B\bar B$ pairs. The longitudinal polarization of decays involving a $J^{PC}=1^{++}$ $\chi_{c1}$ meson is found to be larger than that with a $1^{--}$ $J/\psi$ or $\psi(2S)$ meson. No direct {\it CP}-violating charge asymmetry is observed.

The study presents the first three-dimensional measurement of the decay amplitudes for the processes \(B\to \psi(2S) K^*\) and \(B\to \chi_{c1} K^*\). These measurements provide new information about the polarization structure and underlying dynamics of these decay modes.

In addition, the analysis includes an updated measurement of the amplitudes for \(B\to J/\psi K^*\) decays, improving upon previous results. By comparing the three charmonium final states, the study investigates how the spin and parity of the charmonium meson affect the polarization of the decay products.

The results are based on data collected with the BaBar detector at the PEP-II storage ring. The data sample corresponds to approximately 232 million \(B\bar B\) pairs, providing a large and precise dataset for studying these rare decay processes.

A key finding is that the longitudinal polarization fraction is larger in decays involving the \(J^{PC}=1^{++}\) \(\chi_{c1}\) meson than in decays involving the \(J^{PC}=1^{--}\) charmonium states \(J/\psi\) or \(\psi(2S)\). This difference suggests that the quantum numbers of the charmonium state play an important role in determining the polarization amplitudes.

The study also searches for direct CP-violating charge asymmetries in these decay channels. No evidence for direct CP violation is observed, as the measured charge asymmetries are consistent with zero within the experimental uncertainties.

Using a data sample corresponding to 232 million \(B\bar B\) pairs collected with the BaBar detector at the PEP-II asymmetric-energy \(e^+e^-\) collider, this study investigates the decay dynamics of several \(B\)-meson decays to charmonium and a \(K^*\) meson. In particular, it presents the first full three-dimensional angular amplitude analysis of the modes \(B\to \psi(2S)K^*\) and \(B\to \chi_{c1}K^*\), and provides an updated measurement of the corresponding amplitudes in \(B\to J/\psi K^*\) decays.

The analysis reconstructs the \(K^*\) through its decay to \(K\pi\) and studies the angular distributions of the final-state particles in order to determine the polarization amplitudes of the vector–vector and axial-vector–vector final states. These amplitudes describe how often the final-state particles are produced with longitudinal or transverse polarization and allow tests of theoretical models of hadronic \(B\)-meson decays.

The measured results show a clear difference between decays involving the axial-vector charmonium state \(\chi_{c1}\), which has quantum numbers \(J^{PC}=1^{++}\), and those involving the vector charmonium states \(J/\psi\) and \(\psi(2S)\), which have \(J^{PC}=1^{--}\). In particular, the decays \(B\to \chi_{c1}K^*\) exhibit a larger longitudinal polarization fraction than the corresponding decays to \(J/\psi K^*\) or \(\psi(2S)K^*\). This indicates that the spin-parity structure of the charmonium state plays an important role in determining the polarization pattern of the decay.

The study also searches for direct CP violation by comparing the decay amplitudes and rates of charged \(B\) mesons and their charge-conjugate partners. Within the experimental uncertainties, no significant charge asymmetry is observed. The results are therefore consistent with the absence of direct CP violation in these decay channels and provide improved experimental input for understanding the dynamics of color-suppressed hadronic \(B\)-meson decays.
outputs.L5:
**BaBar: The Experiment That Explored the Matter–Antimatter Mystery**

BaBar was a major particle physics experiment based at the SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory in California. The experiment was designed to study the behavior of subatomic particles called B mesons, which are produced when electrons and positrons collide at very high energies. Its name, “BaBar,” refers to a pair of particles known as B and anti-B mesons.

The main goal of BaBar was to investigate why the universe is made mostly of matter rather than equal amounts of matter and antimatter. According to the laws of physics, the Big Bang should have created matter and antimatter in nearly equal quantities. However, antimatter is now extremely rare. BaBar helped scientists study a phenomenon called **CP violation**, which describes small differences in how matter and antimatter behave.

The BaBar detector collected huge amounts of data from particle collisions. By analyzing these collisions, researchers were able to make precise measurements that improved our understanding of the Standard Model of particle physics. The results from BaBar contributed significantly to confirming theories about CP violation and helped support the work that led to the Nobel Prize in Physics awarded to Makoto Kobayashi and Toshihide Maskawa.

Although the BaBar experiment stopped collecting data in 2008, its scientific impact continues. The data it gathered is still valuable, and its discoveries remain important in the ongoing search to understand the deepest laws of the universe.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a concise abstract for a BaBar physics paper measuring decay amplitudes in \(B\to (J/\psi,\psi(2S),\chi_{c1})K^*\) channels using 232 million \(B\bar B\) pairs, including polarization and CP asymmetry results.
counterfactuals.output: We present an angular analysis of \(B\to (J/\psi,\psi(2S),\chi_{c1})K^*\) decays using a sample of \(232\times10^{6}\) \(B\bar B\) pairs collected with the BABAR detector at the \(\Upsilon(4S)\). The transversity amplitudes and relative phases are measured for charged and neutral \(K^*\) final states. For \(B\to J/\psi K^*\) we find a longitudinal polarization fraction of about \(0.56\) and a sizable \(CP\)-odd transverse component of about \(0.23\), consistent with previous measurements. The corresponding polarization fractions in \(B\to\psi(2S)K^*\) and \(B\to\chi_{c1}K^*\) are also determined, with no evidence for anomalous behavior within uncertainties. Comparisons of \(B\) and \(\bar B\) amplitudes yield direct \(CP\)-violating asymmetries and triple-product asymmetries consistent with zero. These results provide improved constraints on the decay dynamics of color-suppressed \(b\to c\bar c s\) transitions and show no significant indication of \(CP\) violation beyond Standard Model expectations.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize the main results of a three-dimensional angular analysis of \(B\to \psi(2S)K^*\), \(B\to \chi_{c1}K^*\), and \(B\to J/\psi K^*\) decays from the BaBar experiment.
counterfactuals.output:
BaBar performed a three-dimensional transversity/angular analysis of the vector–vector decays  
\[
B\to \psi(2S)K^*,\qquad B\to \chi_{c1}K^*,\qquad B\to J/\psi K^*
\]
using \(K^*\to K\pi\) modes, extracting the polarization amplitudes \(A_0\), \(A_\parallel\), and \(A_\perp\) and their relative phases.

Main results:

- **For \(B\to J/\psi K^*\)**, BaBar measured a sizeable longitudinal component and comparable transverse components:
  \[
  |A_0|^2 \simeq 0.56,\qquad |A_\parallel|^2 \simeq 0.21,\qquad |A_\perp|^2 \simeq 0.23 .
  \]
  The relative phases were significantly different from the simple factorization expectations of \(0\) or \(\pi\), indicating nontrivial final-state interactions.

- **For \(B\to \psi(2S)K^*\)**, the polarization pattern was broadly similar to \(J/\psi K^*\):
  \[
  |A_0|^2 \simeq 0.5,\qquad |A_\parallel|^2 \simeq 0.2,\qquad |A_\perp|^2 \simeq 0.3 ,
  \]
  within larger uncertainties. This supported the idea that the two charmonium vector states have similar decay dynamics in these modes.

- **For \(B\to \chi_{c1}K^*\)**, BaBar found a much larger longitudinal polarization fraction:
  \[
  |A_0|^2 \simeq 0.75\text{--}0.8,
  \]
  with a small CP-odd transverse component \( |A_\perp|^2 \), consistent with being near zero within uncertainties. This made the \(\chi_{c1}K^*\) polarization pattern notably different from the vector-charmonium modes.

- The **CP-odd fraction**, given by \( |A_\perp|^2 \), was about one quarter for \(J/\psi K^*\) and \(\psi(2S)K^*\), but much smaller for \(\chi_{c1}K^*\).

- BaBar also compared \(B\) and \(\bar B\) amplitudes and phases and found **no evidence for direct CP violation**; CP-violating asymmetries and T-odd/triple-product asymmetries were consistent with zero.

Overall, the analysis showed that \(J/\psi K^*\) and \(\psi(2S)K^*\) have similar polarization structures, while \(\chi_{c1}K^*\) is dominantly longitudinally polarized. The measured phases provided evidence for final-state interaction effects beyond naive factorization.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a short particle-physics conference proceeding statement about BaBar’s measurement of amplitudes in \(B\) meson decays to charmonium plus \(K^*\), mentioning the PEP-II dataset size and key findings.
counterfactuals.output:
BABAR has performed an angular-amplitude analysis of \(B\)-meson decays to charmonium plus a \(K^{*}\), using the PEP-II \(e^{+}e^{-}\) dataset corresponding to about \(232\times 10^{6}\) \(B\bar B\) pairs collected at the \(\Upsilon(4S)\). The study reconstructs modes such as  
\[
B \to J/\psi K^{*},\quad B \to \psi(2S)K^{*},\quad B \to \chi_{c1}K^{*},
\]
and extracts the transversity amplitudes and relative phases through fits to the decay angular distributions.

The measurements show sizeable longitudinal and transverse polarization components, with the \(J/\psi K^{*}\) amplitudes determined with high precision. The relative phases are found to differ significantly from the naïve factorization expectation of 0 or \(\pi\), indicating the presence of final-state interactions. The polarization pattern in \(B\to \chi_{c1}K^{*}\) is observed to differ from that in \(J/\psi K^{*}\) and \(\psi(2S)K^{*}\). No evidence for direct \(CP\) violation is observed; the measured \(CP\)-violating asymmetries are consistent with zero within uncertainties. These results provide important tests of factorization and hadronic dynamics in color-suppressed \(B\) decays.

counterfactuals.prompt: Provide a LaTeX-style abstract for an experimental high-energy physics paper reporting polarization amplitudes and direct CP asymmetries in \(B\to c\bar c K^*\) decays.
counterfactuals.output:
```latex
\begin{abstract}
We report measurements of the polarization amplitudes and direct $C\!P$-violating charge asymmetries in the decays
$B \to c\bar{c} K^{*}$, where the charmonium state is reconstructed in
$J/\psi$ and $\psi(2S)$ final states and the $K^{*}$ meson is reconstructed in
$K\pi$ modes. The analysis is based on a data sample corresponding to
$N_{B\bar{B}}$ $B\bar{B}$ pairs collected at the $\Upsilon(4S)$ resonance.
Signal yields are extracted using fits to the beam-energy substituted mass,
energy difference, and event-shape variables, while the polarization parameters
are determined from a transversity angular analysis.

The longitudinal and transverse polarization fractions, expressed in terms of
the transversity amplitudes $A_{0}$, $A_{\parallel}$, and $A_{\perp}$, are
measured together with the relative strong phases
$\arg(A_{\parallel}/A_{0})$ and $\arg(A_{\perp}/A_{0})$.
The results are consistent with previous measurements and with the expectation
that the $C\!P$-odd component is dominated by the perpendicular amplitude
$A_{\perp}$. We also measure the direct charge asymmetries
\[
  A_{C\!P} =
  \frac{\Gamma(\bar{B}\to c\bar{c}\,\bar{K}^{*})
        - \Gamma(B\to c\bar{c}\,K^{*})}
       {\Gamma(\bar{B}\to c\bar{c}\,\bar{K}^{*})
        + \Gamma(B\to c\bar{c}\,K^{*})}
\]
for the charged and neutral decay modes. No significant evidence for direct
$C\!P$ violation is observed. These measurements provide tests of factorization
in color-suppressed $B$ decays and improve the experimental constraints on the
polarization structure of $B\to c\bar{c}K^{*}$ transitions.
\end{abstract}
```

counterfactuals.output: BaBar performed an updated full angular (three-dimensional transversity) analysis of \(B\to J/\psi K^*\) and, for the first time, measured the decay amplitudes in the same way for \(B\to \psi(2S)K^*\) and \(B\to \chi_{c1}K^*\), extracting the longitudinal, parallel, and perpendicular polarization components and their relative phases. The updated \(B\to J/\psi K^*\) results were consistent with previous measurements, with a longitudinal polarization fraction of about one half, and the \(B\to \psi(2S)K^*\) amplitudes were found to be broadly similar to those in \(J/\psi K^*\). In contrast, \(B\to \chi_{c1}K^*\) showed a notably larger longitudinal component, with \(f_L=|A_0|^2\) around \(0.8\), while the perpendicular component was small. Thus BaBar concluded that the two vector-charmonium modes, \(J/\psi K^*\) and \(\psi(2S)K^*\), have compatible polarization patterns, but \( \chi_{c1}K^*\) is significantly more longitudinally polarized.
